Confirm a mature 2.1–3.2 mm spikelet and leaf-base/collar before calling D. commutatum.

best_field_traits: Perennial; unlike many rosette-grasses it may lack an obvious winter basal rosette.
Largest stem blades commonly 6–12 cm long and roughly 7–15 mm wide; often cordate at the base, but not consistently.
Sheath backs often hairless or sparsely hairy; marginal and collar hairs may still be conspicuous.
True ligule a minute fringe or absent; inspect at magnification.
Open, rather few-spikeleted spring panicles; spikelets broadly about 2.1–3.2 mm long.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Stem blade base carefully flattened showing true cordate versus tapering attachment with 1-mm scale
Blade/sheath collar clearly spread showing minute or absent true ligule independently from margin cilia
One intact spring flowering panicle and same rooted shoot
Three mature 2.1–3.2 mm spikelets with calibrated mm ruler, glume details; existing flowering parts already covered

confused_with: other Dichanthelium species (not yet represented in this learner)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Against tiny-spikeleted D. lindheimeri (~1.3–1.6 mm) check actual size and hair ligule; against D. oligosanthes (~2.9–4 mm) compare broad sometimes cordate stem leaf base and very short/absent true ligule; against D. pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm) compare broader stem leaves vs narrow blades and extremely short 0.25–0.5 mm collar fringe. All photos source-determined, not Hays vouchers.
comparisons.photo_context: Four real already archived source-labelled images are incorporated into a genus comparison. The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.
not_reliable_alone: Airy panicle silhouette in a single season
Habitat or presumed annual/perennial condition from clipped stem
Ligule hair lengths or spikelet sizes inferred from photos without rulers
The older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri name interpreted as a new separate species

field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Panicles often overlap. Show spring/autumn phase, true leaf collar, and at least three mature measured spikelets from the same plant before a firm species call.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The literature-size figures and diagnostic leaf features are not verified by the stored photos. Do not attach falsely precise or microscopic arrows.
